anchor.observation: Paul says flesh and blood cannot inherit imperishability, describes trumpet and change, cites victory sayings, gives thanks, and calls for steadfast work.

left.observation: The narrator distinguishes many unrecorded signs from the selected written signs and states the intended relation to belief and life.

left.excerpt: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
left.observation: Two women come at dawn; an angel descends, the guard trembles, the women see the place, run with fear and joy, and meet Jesus.

right.title: Mary turns from the tomb when Jesus calls her name
right.excerpt: But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,
right.observation: Mary weeps, sees two angels, mistakes Jesus for the gardener, recognizes him when named, and carries his message to the disciples.

capsuleTopic.title: Resurrection
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Hope · prediction · tomb · appearances · witness · raised life
capsuleTopic.orientation: Enter the Resurrection through earlier Jewish hope and four distinct Gospel witnesses, then inspect recognition, meals, commissions, post-ascension encounters, public proclamation, bodily hope, and later Scripture memory. The sources remain connected without being merged into one unreported chronology.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Follow earlier hope and prediction into the tomb witnesses, appearances, recognition, sending, ascension, post-ascension sight and address, public proclamation, letter reasoning, and future bodily hope. Keep every Scripture witness in its own wording and sequence.

passages.title: Seven brothers face death with a stated hope
passages.excerpt: It came to pass that seven brothers and their mother were at the king’s command taken and shamefully handled with scourges and cords, to compel them to taste of the abominable s…
passages.observation: A mother and her sons endure torture; the second and fourth brothers speak of receiving life again and being raised by God.

passages.title: A collection for the dead is tied to resurrection hope
passages.excerpt: Judas gathered his army and came to the city of Adullam. As the seventh day was coming on, they purified themselves according to the custom, and kept the Sabbath there.
passages.observation: After hidden sacred objects are found on fallen soldiers, Judas gathers money for an offering and the narrator explicitly connects the act with resurrection.

passages.title: The dead are promised release from their tombs
passages.excerpt: I will raise those who are dead up again from their places, and bring them out from their tombs, for I recognize my name in them.
passages.observation: The speaker promises to raise the dead from their places and later connects burial care with a place in the resurrection.

passages.title: Martyrdom is remembered through immortality and enduring life
passages.excerpt: If it were lawful for us to paint as on a tablet the religion of your story, the spectators wouldn’t shudder at seeing the mother of seven children enduring for the sake of reli…
passages.observation: The discourse remembers the mother and seven sons, describes their contest before the tyrant, and contrasts the tyrant’s punishment with the brothers’ enduring life and honor before God.

passages.title: A written hope of seeing God beyond bodily loss
passages.excerpt: “Oh that my words were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!
passages.observation: Job asks that his words be inscribed and speaks of a living redeemer and of seeing God after bodily destruction.

passages.title: The faithful one is not abandoned to Sheol
passages.excerpt: I have set the LORD always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.
passages.observation: The psalmist speaks of bodily security, refusal of abandonment to Sheol, preservation from decay, and a path of life.

passages.title: Death swallowed and tears wiped away
passages.excerpt: In this mountain, the LORD of Armies will make all peoples a feast of choice meat, a feast of choice wines, of choice meat full of marrow, of well refined choice wines.
passages.observation: A feast for peoples is joined to the removal of a covering, the swallowing of death, wiped tears, and waited-for salvation.

passages.title: The dead live and dust dwellers awake
passages.excerpt: Your dead shall live. Their dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed s…
passages.observation: The passage addresses the dead as living, summons those in dust to awake, and then speaks of hidden waiting while judgment passes.

passages.title: Those sleeping in dust awake to divided outcomes
passages.excerpt: “At that time Michael will stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there will be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation…
passages.observation: A time of distress, deliverance, awakening from dust, differing outcomes, and sealed words are placed together.

passages.title: Dry bones live and opened graves become restoration language
passages.excerpt: The LORD’s hand was on me, and he brought me out in the LORD’s Spirit, and set me down in the middle of the valley; and it was full of bones.
passages.observation: Ezekiel sees dry bones receive sinews, flesh, breath, and life; the vision is then identified with Israel’s lost hope and a promise of opened graves, Spirit, land, and restored life.

passages.title: Ransom from Sheol becomes a taunt against death
passages.excerpt: The guilt of Ephraim is stored up. His sin is stored up.
passages.observation: After stored guilt and delayed birth imagery, the speech asks whether Ephraim will be ransomed from Sheol and redeemed from death, then addresses death and Sheol directly.

passages.title: Jonah prays from the depths and returns to dry land
passages.excerpt: Then Jonah prayed to the LORD, his God, out of the fish’s belly.
passages.observation: Jonah’s prayer recalls distress, Sheol, descent, templeward attention, and a life brought up before the fish releases him.

passages.title: The sign of Jonah names three days and judgment
passages.excerpt: Then certain of the scribes and Pharisees answered, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
passages.observation: Jesus answers a demand for a sign by naming Jonah’s three days, the Son of Man’s three days, and future witnesses in judgment.

passages.title: Jerusalem, death, and third-day raising enter the disclosure
passages.excerpt: From that time, Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and the third d…
passages.observation: Jesus begins to show the disciples a sequence of Jerusalem, suffering, killing, raising, Peter’s resistance, and a call to follow.

passages.title: Delivery, killing, raising, and sorrow in Galilee
passages.excerpt: While they were staying in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men,
passages.observation: Jesus states delivery into human hands, killing, and third-day raising while the disciples respond with great sorrow.

passages.title: The road prediction ends with third-day raising
passages.excerpt: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside, and on the way he said to them,
passages.observation: On the way to Jerusalem, Jesus names condemnation, delivery, mockery, scourging, crucifixion, and raising.

passages.title: Scattering is followed by a promised meeting in Galilee
passages.excerpt: Then Jesus said to them, “All of you will be made to stumble because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’
passages.observation: After the meal, Jesus cites the struck shepherd, predicts the disciples’ scattering, and says he will go before them into Galilee after rising.

passages.title: A concealed journey and an unasked question
passages.excerpt: They went out from there and passed through Galilee. He didn’t want anyone to know it,
passages.observation: Passing through Galilee, Jesus teaches delivery, killing, and rising; the disciples do not understand and are afraid to ask.

passages.title: A detailed prediction names rising after three days
passages.excerpt: They were on the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going in front of them, and they were amazed; and those who followed were afraid. He again took the twelve, and began…
passages.observation: Going toward Jerusalem, Jesus names leaders, Gentiles, mockery, abuse, death, and rising after three days.

passages.title: Galilee is named beyond scattering and denial
passages.excerpt: When they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
passages.observation: After the hymn, Jesus predicts scattering and a later meeting in Galilee; Peter and the others answer with claims of loyalty.

passages.title: Prophetic fulfillment is stated but not understood
passages.excerpt: He took the twelve aside and said to them, “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things that are written through the prophets about the Son of Man will be comp…
passages.observation: Jesus takes the Twelve, links the coming sequence to the prophets, names Gentile treatment, death, and third-day rising, while understanding remains hidden.

passages.title: Temple language is remembered after resurrection
passages.excerpt: The Passover of the Jews was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
passages.observation: After the temple action, Jesus answers a sign demand with a destroyed-and-raised temple saying; the narrator identifies the body and later disciple memory.

passages.title: Life-giving authority and two resurrection outcomes
passages.excerpt: Jesus therefore answered them, “Most certainly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father doing. For whatever things he does, these the Son also…
passages.observation: Jesus speaks of the Son giving life, an approaching hour, graves opening to his voice, and resurrection to life or judgment.

passages.title: The shepherd lays down his life and speaks of taking it again
passages.excerpt: I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and I’m known by my own;
passages.observation: Jesus joins knowing the sheep, one flock, the Father’s love, voluntary self-giving, authority to lay life down, and authority to take it again.

passages.title: Martha names the last day; Jesus names resurrection and life
passages.excerpt: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.
passages.observation: At Bethany, Martha speaks of future resurrection, and Jesus answers with a first-person claim before asking whether she believes.

passages.title: Absence is followed by sight and shared life
passages.excerpt: I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.
passages.observation: Jesus says he will not leave the disciples orphaned, contrasts the world’s coming inability to see him with the disciples’ sight, and connects his life with theirs.

passages.title: A little while separates absence, sight, sorrow, and joy
passages.excerpt: “A little while, and you will not see me. Again a little while, and you will see me.”
passages.observation: Jesus repeats that the disciples will not see and then will see, hears their uncertainty, and compares their coming sorrow and joy to childbirth before promising to see them again.

passages.title: A resurrection question is answered from Moses
passages.excerpt: On that day Sadducees (those who say that there is no resurrection) came to him. They asked him,
passages.observation: Sadducees pose a seven-brother case; Jesus addresses the age to come, divine power, and God’s words at the bush.

passages.title: Children of resurrection can die no more
passages.excerpt: Some of the Sadducees came to him, those who deny that there is a resurrection.
passages.observation: Sadducees present the seven-brother case; Jesus distinguishes this age from the coming age and cites Moses at the bush.

passages.title: A sealed and guarded tomb anticipates the third day
passages.excerpt: Now on the next day, which was the day after the Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees were gathered together to Pilate,
passages.observation: Chief priests and Pharisees recall Jesus’ rising claim, ask Pilate to secure the tomb, seal the stone, and post a guard.

passages.title: Earthquake, messenger, empty place, and a meeting on the road
passages.excerpt: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
passages.observation: Two women come at dawn; an angel descends, the guard trembles, the women see the place, run with fear and joy, and meet Jesus.

passages.title: The guard report becomes a purchased explanation
passages.excerpt: Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
passages.observation: Some guards report to the chief priests, money is given, a disciples-stole-the-body account is instructed, and protection from the governor is promised.

passages.title: Worship, doubt, authority, and commission in Galilee
passages.excerpt: But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
passages.observation: The eleven go to the appointed mountain, see Jesus, worship while some doubt, and receive a commission grounded in his authority and presence.

passages.title: Three women, a moved stone, and a young man’s announcement
passages.excerpt: When the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices, that they might come and anoint him.
passages.observation: Three women bring spices, find the stone moved, see a young man, hear that Jesus is risen, and flee trembling and astonished.

passages.title: Reports are disbelieved before Jesus appears to the eleven
passages.excerpt: Now when he had risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
passages.observation: Jesus appears first to Mary Magdalene, then in another form to two travelers, and finally rebukes the eleven’s unbelief.

passages.title: Women remember the saying; apostles call the report nonsense
passages.excerpt: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they and some others came to the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared.
passages.observation: Women find the stone rolled away and the body absent, hear two men recall Jesus’ prediction, remember, report to the apostles, and Peter runs to the tomb.

passages.title: Travelers recognize Jesus in the breaking of bread
passages.excerpt: Behold, two of them were going that very day to a village named Emmaus, which was sixty stadia from Jerusalem.
passages.observation: Two travelers recount recent events and the women’s report; Jesus interprets Scripture, is recognized at the meal, disappears, and they return.

passages.title: Peace, wounds, food, Scripture, and promised power
passages.excerpt: As they said these things, Jesus himself stood among them, and said to them, “Peace be to you.”
passages.observation: Jesus appears among the gathered group, invites examination, eats fish, opens Scripture, names witness, and promises power from on high.

passages.title: Blessing continues as Jesus is carried into heaven
passages.excerpt: He led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
passages.observation: Jesus leads the disciples toward Bethany, blesses them, is carried into heaven, and they return to Jerusalem with joy and worship.

passages.title: Mary reports; two disciples run; cloths are seen
passages.excerpt: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb.
passages.observation: Mary sees the removed stone and reports; Peter and the other disciple run, enter in different order, inspect the linen, and return.

passages.title: Mary turns from the tomb when Jesus calls her name
passages.excerpt: But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,
passages.observation: Mary weeps, sees two angels, mistakes Jesus for the gardener, recognizes him when named, and carries his message to the disciples.

passages.title: Locked doors, shown wounds, breath, and sending
passages.excerpt: When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and sto…
passages.observation: Jesus comes among disciples behind locked doors, speaks peace, shows wounds, sends them, breathes, and speaks of forgiveness.

passages.title: Thomas moves from demanded evidence to confession
passages.excerpt: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came.
passages.observation: Thomas rejects the first report, names the evidence he requires, encounters Jesus eight days later, and answers with a confession.

passages.title: Selected signs are written for belief and life
passages.excerpt: Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;
passages.observation: The narrator distinguishes many unrecorded signs from the selected written signs and states the intended relation to belief and life.

passages.title: A catch, a charcoal fire, and recognition by the sea
passages.excerpt: After these things, Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way.
passages.observation: Jesus reveals himself by the Sea of Tiberias through a catch of fish, a shore meal, and recognition among seven disciples.

passages.title: Peter is questioned, commissioned, and redirected from comparison
passages.excerpt: So when they had eaten their breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affect…
passages.observation: After breakfast Jesus questions Peter three times, commands care for his sheep, speaks of Peter’s death, addresses the beloved disciple, and closes with testimony.

passages.title: Forty days, kingdom instruction, witness, and ascension
passages.excerpt: The first book I wrote, Theophilus, concerned all that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
passages.observation: Luke summarizes appearances over forty days, teaching, table instruction, promised Spirit, expanding witness, ascension, and the words of two men.

passages.title: Received tradition names burial, raising, and appearances
passages.excerpt: Now I declare to you, brothers, the Good News which I preached to you, which also you received, in which you also stand,
passages.observation: Paul recalls the message received and delivered: death, burial, third-day raising, and appearances to Cephas, the Twelve, many others, James, apostles, and Paul.

passages.title: Peter names raising, witness, exaltation, and Psalm language
passages.excerpt: “Men of Israel, hear these words! Jesus of Nazareth, a man approved by God to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which God did by him among you, even as you yourselves know,
passages.observation: At Pentecost Peter moves from Jesus’ deeds and death to God’s raising, David’s psalm, apostolic witness, exaltation, Spirit, and lordship.

passages.title: The Prince of life is raised and the apostles are witnesses
passages.excerpt: When Peter saw it, he responded to the people, “You men of Israel, why do you marvel at this man? Why do you fasten your eyes on us, as though by our own power or godliness we h…
passages.observation: After a healing, Peter contrasts the audience’s actions with God’s raising, names witness, prophetic fulfillment, restoration, and the raised servant sent first.

passages.title: Resurrection proclamation is questioned before the council
passages.excerpt: As they spoke to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came to them,
passages.observation: Priests and Sadducees react to resurrection teaching; Peter explains the healed man through the crucified and raised Jesus and names salvation.

passages.title: The council hears of raising, exaltation, repentance, and witness
passages.excerpt: When they had brought them, they set them before the council. The high priest questioned them,
passages.observation: The high priest charges the apostles; Peter answers by naming human killing, divine raising and exaltation, repentance, forgiveness, and witnesses.

passages.title: Stephen sees Jesus standing at God’s right hand
passages.excerpt: Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed at him with their teeth.
passages.observation: As the council reacts, Stephen sees God’s glory and Jesus standing at God’s right hand, names what he sees, is driven out and stoned, and addresses Jesus while dying.

passages.title: Saul encounters Jesus and begins proclaiming him
passages.excerpt: But Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest
passages.observation: A heavenly light and voice interrupt Saul near Damascus; Jesus identifies himself, Ananias receives instructions, Saul regains sight and is baptized, and he begins proclaiming Jesus.

passages.title: Chosen witnesses eat and drink with the risen Jesus
passages.excerpt: Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism;
passages.observation: Peter recounts Jesus’ public ministry, death, third-day raising, restricted appearances, table fellowship, commission, judgment, prophets, and forgiveness.

passages.title: No decay, many-day appearances, and synagogue announcement
passages.excerpt: “Brothers, children of the stock of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, the word of this salvation is sent out to you.
passages.observation: Paul recounts condemnation, burial, divine raising, appearances, psalm and prophetic words, forgiveness, and justification.

passages.title: Paul argues in Thessalonica that the Christ had to rise
passages.excerpt: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
passages.observation: Across three Sabbaths Paul reasons from Scripture that the Christ had to suffer and rise, identifies Jesus as the Christ, and receives mixed responses that lead to public disturbance.

passages.title: Jesus and resurrection are heard as foreign deities in Athens
passages.excerpt: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw the city full of idols.
passages.observation: Paul converses in Athens, is brought to the Areopagus, speaks of the unknown God, creation, judgment, and raising; hearers mock, defer, or join him.

passages.title: Paul retells the Damascus encounter before a Jerusalem crowd
passages.excerpt: “As I made my journey and came close to Damascus, about noon suddenly a great light shone around me from the sky.
passages.observation: Paul recounts the noon light, Jesus’ voice, blindness, Ananias’s words, restored sight, baptism, a later temple vision, and a commission toward the nations.

passages.title: Paul names a shared hope of resurrection in his defense
passages.excerpt: When the governor had beckoned to him to speak, Paul answered, “Because I know that you have been a judge of this nation for many years, I cheerfully make my defense,
passages.observation: Before Felix, Paul describes worship, Law and Prophets, a resurrection of just and unjust, conscience, and the single statement made before the council.

passages.title: Festus summarizes a dispute about a dead Jesus said to be alive
passages.excerpt: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea and greeted Festus.
passages.observation: Festus explains Paul’s case to Agrippa as a religious dispute centered on Jesus, who had died and whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

passages.title: Promise to the fathers frames the question of raised dead
passages.excerpt: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.
passages.observation: Paul asks Agrippa to hear his defense, locates his hope in the promise to the fathers, and asks why God raising the dead is judged incredible.

passages.title: Paul connects the heavenly appearance with his public witness
passages.excerpt: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,
passages.observation: Paul recounts the light and voice on the Damascus road, Jesus’ identification and commission, his response before changing audiences, and the prophetic claim that the risen Christ proclaims light.

passages.title: Davidic descent and resurrection power open the letter
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, set apart for the Good News of God,
passages.observation: Paul introduces the good news as promised beforehand and names Jesus through Davidic descent and declaration as Son of God in power by resurrection.

passages.title: Abraham’s credited faith is extended to those trusting the raiser of Jesus
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: Now it was not written that it was accounted to him for his sake alone,
passages.observation: Paul moves from words written about Abraham to later readers who believe in the God who raised Jesus, then pairs delivery and raising with trespasses and justification.

passages.title: Raised life reshapes the argument about sin
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound?
passages.observation: Paul connects baptism with death, burial, resurrection, newness of life, freedom from dominion, bodily presentation, and grace.

passages.title: Union with the raised Christ is linked to fruit for God
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: Or don’t you know, brothers (for I speak to men who know the law), that the law has dominion over a man for as long as he lives?
passages.observation: Paul uses marriage and death-to-law language before saying the readers belong to the one raised from the dead so that they may bear fruit for God and serve in newness of Spirit.

passages.title: The indwelling Spirit is linked to mortal bodies receiving life
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if it is so that the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if any man doesn’t have the Spirit of Christ, he is not his.
passages.observation: Paul distinguishes flesh and Spirit and says the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus will give life to mortal bodies.

passages.title: The word is near; Christ need not be brought up from the dead
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: But the righteousness which is of faith says this, “Don’t say in your heart, ‘Who will ascend into heaven?’ (that is, to bring Christ down);
passages.observation: Paul adapts ascent and descent questions, names bringing Christ down or up from the dead, then places the proclaimed word near the hearer and joins confession, belief, righteousness, and salvation.

passages.title: If Christ is not raised, the argument collapses; but Christ is first fruit
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: Now if Christ is preached, that he has been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
passages.observation: Paul tests denial of resurrection through consequences for Christ, preaching, witness, faith, sins, and the dead, then turns to first fruit, order, reign, and the last enemy.

passages.title: Practice and danger are questioned if the dead are not raised
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: Or else what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead aren’t raised at all, why then are they baptized for the dead?
passages.observation: Paul asks about baptism for the dead, his own danger, a quoted slogan, corrupting company, sobriety, and knowledge of God.

passages.title: Seed, bodies, Adam, and transformed likeness answer the body question
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised?” and, “With what kind of body do they come?”
passages.observation: Paul answers how the dead are raised with seed imagery, differentiated bodies, contrasts of sowing and raising, two Adams, and heavenly likeness.

passages.title: Trumpet, transformation, victory, and steadfast work close the chapter
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: Now I say this, brothers, that flesh and blood can’t inherit God’s Kingdom; neither does the perishable inherit imperishable.
passages.observation: Paul says flesh and blood cannot inherit imperishability, describes trumpet and change, cites victory sayings, gives thanks, and calls for steadfast work.

passages.title: Mortal pressure and Jesus’ life are held together
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: But we have this treasure in clay vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God and not from ourselves.
passages.observation: Paul describes treasure in clay vessels, affliction without abandonment, carrying Jesus’ dying, manifested life, and confidence that the raiser of Jesus will present the speakers with the readers.

passages.title: The one who died and rose redirects the lives of others
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: For the love of Christ compels us; because we judge thus: that one died for all, therefore all died.
passages.observation: Paul says Christ’s love compels a judgment about one dying for all, then says Christ died and rose so that the living no longer live for themselves before naming new creation.

passages.title: Resurrection power leads to enthronement and a body image
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: For this cause I also, having heard of the faith in the Lord Jesus which is among you and the love which you have toward all the saints,
passages.observation: A prayer for enlightened understanding names hope, inheritance, power, raising, seating above rulers, subjection, headship, and the assembly as Christ’s body.

passages.title: Made alive and raised together amid a before-and-after account
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: You were made alive when you were dead in transgressions and sins,
passages.observation: Readers are described as dead in trespasses, following hostile powers, then made alive, raised, and seated with Christ by mercy and grace for good works.

passages.title: Knowing resurrection power reaches toward transformed bodies
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: However, I consider those things that were gain to me as a loss for Christ.
passages.observation: Paul counts former gains as loss, seeks to know Christ and resurrection power amid suffering, presses toward a goal, and ends with citizenship and bodily transformation.

passages.title: The firstborn from the dead stands within a cosmic sequence
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
passages.observation: Christ is named image, creator, sustainer, head, beginning, and firstborn from the dead before the passage speaks of fullness, reconciliation, and peace through the cross.

passages.title: Buried and raised with Christ while the record is removed
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: For in him all the fullness of the Deity dwells bodily,
passages.observation: Paul joins fullness in Christ, circumcision imagery, burial and raising in baptism, forgiveness, cancellation of a hostile record, and disarming rulers.

passages.title: The dead in Christ rise before the gathered meeting
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: But we don’t want you to be ignorant, brothers, about those who have fallen asleep, so that you don’t grieve like the rest, who have no hope.
passages.observation: Paul addresses grief, grounds hope in Jesus’ death and rising, describes the Lord’s descent, the dead rising, the living gathered, and mutual comfort.

passages.title: Remember the risen descendant of David
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: Remember Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, of the offspring of David, according to my Good News,
passages.observation: Paul commands remembrance of Jesus Christ risen from the dead and descended from David, then connects imprisonment, endurance, dying, living, reigning, denial, and faithfulness.

passages.title: A claim that resurrection is past is named as error
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: Remind them of these things, charging them in the sight of the Lord that they don’t argue about words to no profit, to the subverting of those who hear.
passages.observation: Timothy is charged to avoid word battles, handle truth accurately, and confront teaching that the resurrection has already happened.

passages.title: Deliverance refused for a better resurrection
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: What more shall I say? For the time would fail me if I told of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets—
passages.observation: A rapid memory of judges, kings, prophets, victories, suffering, death, wandering, and unreceived promise includes women receiving dead and others seeking a better resurrection.

passages.title: The God of peace brings the great shepherd from the dead
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: Now may the God of peace, who brought again from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep with the blood of an eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,
passages.observation: The benediction names the God of peace, Jesus as great shepherd, covenant blood, being made complete, God’s work, and glory.

passages.title: Living hope begins with Jesus’ resurrection
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ fro…
passages.observation: Peter blesses God for new birth into living hope through resurrection, an imperishable inheritance, guarded faith, testing, unseen love, joy, and salvation.

passages.title: Resurrection, baptism, heaven, and subjected powers
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: Because Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring you to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit,
passages.observation: Christ’s suffering, death and life, proclamation, Noah, baptism, resurrection, ascension, and subjected powers are gathered into one dense sequence.

passages.title: Firstborn from the dead appears in a greeting
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: John, to the seven assemblies that are in Asia: Grace to you and peace from God, who is and who was and who is to come; and from the seven Spirits who are before his throne;
passages.observation: John’s greeting names Jesus as faithful witness, firstborn from the dead, ruler, one who loves and frees by blood, and the coming one.

passages.title: The living one was dead and holds the keys
passages.excerpt: When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead man. He laid his right hand on me, saying, “Don’t be afraid. I am the first and the last,
passages.observation: The visionary falls; Jesus touches him, commands him not to fear, identifies himself as first and last and living, and names keys, writing, stars, and lampstands.

passages.title: The one who was dead and lived addresses Smyrna
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: “To the angel of the assembly in Smyrna write: “The first and the last, who was dead, and has come to life says these things:
passages.observation: The message names Jesus as first and last who was dead and lived, then addresses affliction, poverty, opposition, imprisonment, faithfulness, crown, and second death.

passages.title: A standing Lamb appears as slain
passages.phase: The risen Christ in the letters
passages.excerpt: I saw in the middle of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the middle of the elders, a Lamb standing, as though it had been slain, having seven horns and seven e…
passages.observation: A Lamb stands as though slain, takes the scroll, and receives a song naming slaughter, blood, purchased peoples, kingdom, and priests.

passages.title: First resurrection, final judgment, and the book of life
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: I saw thrones, and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them. I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and such…
passages.observation: The vision describes enthroned witnesses, a first resurrection, the rest of the dead, released deception, a great white throne, opened books, and the second death.

passages.title: A new creation is described where death is no more
passages.phase: Bodies, hope, and the final horizon
passages.excerpt: I saw a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth have passed away, and the sea is no more.
passages.observation: John sees a new heaven, new earth, and new Jerusalem; a throne voice announces God dwelling with people, tears removed, death ended, and all things made new before a second-death warning.
